title: SlideCast Studio v4.4 “BLOOM”
subtitle: Update — redesigned settings, presets, 4:5 / 4:3 and Gemini 3.8 TTS
description: SlideCast Studio v4.4 BLOOM tidies up the settings screen, adds direct dragging on the preview, rebuilt presets, 4:5 and 4:3 aspect ratios, and Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS with its voice library and your own custom voices.
author: aokuma
hero_alt: SlideCast Studio v4.4 BLOOM — Settings, without the guesswork.

Voice library and your own voices

blocks.title: 🌐 About the screenshots
blocks.text: The interface screenshots on this page use the Japanese edition. The captions explain the relevant controls, and key labels are given in English.

blocks.html:
SlideCast Studio is now at v4.4 “BLOOM”.

v4.3 “RENDER” added a high-quality, frame-by-frame export so that videos come out cleanly whatever your PC is doing. This release focuses on rebuilding the settings screen so you can set things up without guesswork, and on support for Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS.

“There are so many settings I don’t know where to start.” “Lining things up with number sliders is tedious.” “I rebuild my settings for every social network.” This update removes those snags one by one. It is also worth a look if you are curious about Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS or want to use a clone of your own voice.

blocks.alt: The Basic tab of the settings screen. Under video size and subtitle layout, 4:5 (Instagram) is selected; undo and redo buttons sit at the bottom
blocks.caption: The Basic tab (基本). 4:5 and 4:3 are new, and undo/redo now sit at the bottom of the settings screen

sections.title: A tidier settings screen
sections.intro: Easy mode is now a switch inside the same settings screen.

blocks.html: Until now, easy mode was a separate “easy settings” panel. From this release, you turn “かんたん” (Easy) on or off inside the same settings screen. Both views edit the same settings, so you can decide the basics in easy mode and then switch to detailed mode to fine-tune.

items.title: Easy ON
items.text: Shows only the settings you use most

blocks.title: 🛠️ Easy mode is still a work in progress
blocks.text: To be honest, easy mode is not yet as simple as it should be. I will keep improving it.

blocks.html: Buttons, switches, sliders and notes that looked slightly different from tab to tab now use the same components everywhere.

blocks.text: Undo and redo, just for settings

blocks.html: The bottom of the settings screen now has undo (Ctrl+Z) and redo (Ctrl+Y) for settings. They are greyed out when there is nothing to undo. Try a different colour or preset, and step straight back if you don’t like it.

blocks.alt: The settings screen with Easy mode on. The undo and redo buttons at the bottom left are outlined in red
blocks.caption: Settings-only undo and redo sit at the bottom left of the settings screen

sections.title: Grab and move things on the preview
sections.intro: Positions and sizes you used to set with number sliders can now be dragged directly on the preview.

items: Slide image: while “スライド画像の配置” (Slide image placement) is open, drag the frame to move it and the corners to scale it
Badges: move and resize the badge selected in the Badge tab. Click a badge on the preview to select it

Character icon and speech bubble: while character settings are open, move the icon and bubble of a speech-bubble character. The matching “Icon” or “Speech bubble” heading opens in the settings as you grab it

blocks.html:
Badges and stickers now snap to each other, stopping neatly at edges and centres, at equal spacing, and at the centre of the screen or image. The Badge tab also has the snap switch, and it shows ON or OFF.

In the Ticker tab, only the ticker you have open scrolls on the preview, so you can check it on its own.

blocks.alt: The editor with the Badge tab open. Move handles appear on a badge and a sticker in the preview
blocks.caption: In the Badge tab you can move badges directly on the preview. Snapping is toggled with the switch at the top right of the tab

sections.title: Presets, rebuilt
sections.intro: Built-in presets are now “platform” plus “subtitle design”, and your own presets can save and apply only the parts you choose.

blocks.text: Built-in presets: platform plus subtitle design

head: Group
Count
Presets

Standard / Outline / Pop / Soft / News / Cinema / Handwritten / Retro

blocks.html: Built-in presets change only the settings they define. BGM, OP/ED, badges and voices stay as they are, so you can pick TikTok as the platform and then Pop as the subtitle design. For portrait platforms, subtitles and slides move to positions less likely to be covered by the app’s captions and buttons.

blocks.text: Choose what your own presets save

items.title: Look
items.text: Screen, background, slide image, subtitles, badges, tickers, OP/ED

blocks.html: Hover over each part to see exactly what is saved. API keys, export settings, background videos and auto-acting are never saved in presets, and they keep their current values when you apply one.

blocks.alt: The Save preset dialog, with checkboxes grouped under look, motion and timing, and sound
blocks.caption: When saving a preset, tick the parts you want to include

blocks.text: Choose what a preset changes when you apply it

blocks.html: The confirmation screen lists the changes grouped by part. Untick a part to keep its current values. A note above the Apply button reminds you that you can undo.

sections.title: New 4:5 and 4:3 aspect ratios
sections.intro: Choose portrait 4:5 for Instagram feeds, or 4:3 for classic slide decks.

blocks.html: The aspect-ratio options now include 4:5 and 4:3. SlideCast Bundle Builder and AI CODE MOVIE STUDIO also gain 4:5 and 4:3 for image ratios and subtitle layouts (a subtitle line holds about 22 Japanese characters at 4:5 and about 24 at 4:3).

blocks.alt: The editor with 4:5 (Instagram) selected in the Basic tab; the preview has become a 4:5 portrait frame
blocks.caption: Choose 4:5 under video size and subtitle layout (動画サイズ・字幕レイアウト) in the Basic tab and the preview switches to 4:5

sections.title: Gemini 3.8 TTS and the voice library
sections.intro: Both the in-app AI voice (Gemini) and SlideCast Bundle Builder can now use Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS / 3.8 Flash Lite TTS.

items.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS
items.text: Works with library voices and your own voices

blocks.text: Search the voice library with the 3.8 models

blocks.html: With a 3.8 model selected, a “ライブラリから探す” (Search the library) button appears next to the voice field (an API key is required).

items: Filter by language, gender, pitch and keyword
Listen to a sample on the spot
Loading the list is free; samples use your API quota

blocks.alt: API settings in the Voice tab, numbered: 1 enter the Gemini API key, 2 select Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, 3 press “Search the library”
blocks.caption: In the Voice tab (音声): 1 enter your API key, 2 choose a Gemini 3.8 model, 3 press “ライブラリから探す” (Search the library)

blocks.alt: The voice library dialog, filtered by language, keyword, gender and pitch, with Listen and Select buttons for each voice
blocks.caption: The voice library. Filter by language, gender, pitch and keyword, and listen on the spot

blocks.html:
Switch the dialog to “自作の音声” (Your voices) to list the voices made in the project behind your API key — voices designed from a prompt, or clones of a voice. You can also type an ID straight into “その他の音声（IDを入力）” (Other voice — enter ID).

Create custom and cloned voices in Google AI Studio itself; generating speech with them works in SlideCast Studio or SlideCast Bundle Builder.

blocks.alt: The “Your voices” tab of the voice library, listing a cloned voice and prompt-designed voices with expiry dates (IDs are blurred)
blocks.caption: Your own and cloned voices. Only voices made in the project behind this API key appear

blocks.title: ⚠️ Please note
blocks.text: Library voices and your own voices work only with Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS / 3.8 Flash Lite TTS. Your own and cloned voices belong to your Google AI Studio project and API key, and appear in the list once that key is entered. Generating speech uses your own API quota and charges, as before. When you create an API key, always set a spending cap and keep the key private.

sections.title: Ticker and badge libraries
sections.intro: Save the tickers and badges you make, and reuse them.

items: Save ticker items and badges to a library and bring them back in other projects or other positions
The ticker library is shared between top and bottom; the badge library is shared across all four corners
Ticker items can be reordered with a drag handle, and switched on or off with a switch

blocks.alt: The badge library dialog, with Apply and Remove from library buttons on a saved badge
blocks.caption: The badge library. Press Apply (適用) to bring a saved badge back

sections.title: Tidier character settings and up to six gestures
sections.intro: The headings now tell you what each part changes.

blocks.html: Character settings are now grouped under Basic → Icon → Speech bubble → Text → Voice.

Icons of newly created characters now have a fixed size that no longer follows the subtitle area, so changing subtitle settings won’t resize them. Existing characters keep working; opening an older character in easy mode moves it to the fixed-size method while keeping its look.
Voice-linked character packs made with MouthLoop can now use up to six gestures (previously three). Existing three-gesture packs work as before.

blocks.alt: The character editor, with headings for basic settings, icon, speech bubble, text and voice settings
blocks.caption: The character editor is now split into headings by part

sections.title: Other improvements and fixes
sections.intro: Smaller usability improvements and bug fixes.

items: Refreshed dashboard, with links to tutorial videos on YouTube, X, the official site and update news (note)
Fixed input dialogs keeping only the last character when you type one character at a time
Fixed text settings not applying to standard-subtitle characters, and large text being cut off at the subtitle area
Swapping a character’s side now mirrors the icon and speech bubble positions correctly
OP/ED settings can be opened and edited while their switch is off
Slide exports (images, PDF, PPTX and so on) and their preview no longer include the top and bottom tickers (video settings are unchanged)
Backups no longer include Gem URLs (older backups still load as before)
The subtitle animation preview plays once when you change the type, then stops
Reorganised the still-slide settings so the help bubbles are no longer clipped
Fixed the dashboard content briefly shifting left after projects load
Existing projects open as they are. Aspect ratios, presets and character settings read your existing data
Presets saved in earlier versions still apply as before. Choosing parts applies to presets you save from now on
Built-in presets now change only the settings they define; they no longer reset BGM or OP/ED to defaults
The voice library and your own voices work only with the 3.8 models. Samples and generation use your API quota

sections.title: Updating to v4.4
sections.intro: If you have already bought SlideCast Studio, copy v4.4 from the same shared link in the paid note article.

blocks.title: 💾 Make a backup first
blocks.text: If you want to keep your existing projects, library and settings, create a backup from “バックアップ” (Backup) on the dashboard before you update.

blocks.html: To update the Apps Script edition in place, the files to replace since v4.3 are “AppBundle.html” and “無題.html” in the v4.4 distribution folder. Copy them into your existing Apps Script project and redeploy the existing deployment as a new version. (code.gs and the files beginning with “GasAsset_” are unchanged in this release.)

blocks.label: Detailed update steps for the Apps Script edition

blocks.html: For the local HTML edition, download “SlideCast Studio v4.4〖ローカル版〗.html” and open it. A new Apps Script project or a different browser will not show your previous data automatically; restore it from a backup in that case.

sections.title: Rethinking how you set up the screen
sections.intro: What you need, when you need it.

blocks.html:
v4.3 “RENDER” let you choose how the screen becomes a video. v4.4 “BLOOM” goes one step earlier and rethinks how you set up that screen. The settings screen is where you spend the most time, so rather than removing options, I rearranged them so that what you need shows up when you need it.

Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS also widens what your narration can sound like. It needs an API key, but it lets you use custom voices and even a clone of your own voice. Setting up the API may feel like a hurdle, but it is well worth trying.

Tutorial videos are being added to the YouTube channel as well.
